# Report on `region.fasta` (locus_006)

**Sequence:** 3,000 bp, single record `>locus_006`; 49.1% G+C (A 756, C 709, G 764, T 771). Coordinates below are **1‑based, inclusive**.

## Summary

The region contains **no evidence of protein-coding function** but does contain **one clearly notable, statistically striking feature: a tandem array of eight near-identical copies of an ~18–20 bp motif, repeated at ~72 bp intervals across ~0.5 kb.**

## Feature 1 — Tandem repeat array (the main finding)

**Location: ~1,962–2,486 (≈525 bp), roughly the middle–3′ portion of the sequence.**

Eight copies of the consensus

```
5'-CGGCTTTGGTTACTAAGG-3'   (18 bp)
```

occur in a head-to-tail array:

| # | Position (1‑based) | Sequence | Mismatches vs. consensus |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1,962–1,979 | CGGCTTTGGTTACTAAGG | 0 |
| 2 | 2,039–2,056 | CGGCTTTT**T**GTTACTAAGG → CGGCTTT**T**GTTACTAAGG | 1 |
| 3 | 2,113–2,130 | CGGCTTTGGTTACTAAGG | 0 |
| 4 | 2,182–2,199 | CGGCTTTGT**TTT**CTAAGG | 2 |
| 5 | 2,256–2,273 | CGGCTTTGGTTACTAAGG | 0 |
| 6 | 2,314–2,331 | CGGCTTTGGT**GA**CTAAGG | 1 |
| 7 | 2,388–2,405 | CGGCTTTGGTTACTAAG**C** | 1 |
| 8 | 2,469–2,486 | CGGGTTTGGTTACTAAGG | 1 |

* Mean period **72.4 bp** (individual spacings 59, 56, 51, 56, 40, 56, 63 bp between motif copies).
* The copies are separated by **40–63 bp of non-homologous sequence**: when the eight 72‑bp units are aligned, overall pairwise identity is 43% (vs. 25.4% ± 1.0% for composition-matched shuffled controls, z ≈ 18), but **once the first ~20 bp of each unit is removed, identity falls to 25.6% — i.e. indistinguishable from random.** All of the detectable repeat structure therefore resides in the conserved ~20‑bp block; the intervening sequence has no residual similarity between copies.
* **Significance:** under any reasonable model this is not chance. An 18-mer allowing ≤3 mismatches has an expected count of ~0.001 in 3 kb; eight copies (six perfect or 1‑mismatch) is a highly significant enrichment.
* The array is the **only** repetitive region in the file. An exhaustive scan (all exact 12-mer-seeded self-alignments, windowed 8-mer Jaccard self-comparison, over-represented k-mer analysis for k = 8–16) found no other repeat ≥30–40 bp anywhere in the 3 kb, and no copies of the motif (or its reverse complement) outside positions 1,962–2,486. Note that a standard tandem-repeat finder would likely *not* call this, because only ~20 of every 72 bp are conserved.

## Feature 2 — No coding potential

* Longest ORF on the plus strand: **1,434–1,599 (165 nt, 54 codons)**; on the minus strand: 2,538–2,667 (129 nt). No ORF approaches gene length.
* Stop codons occur at essentially the random expectation in all six reading frames (47–54 per 1,000 codons vs. 46.9 expected), and the longest stop-free stretch (258 nt plus strand at 708; 276 nt minus strand at 1,624) is what is expected for non-coding DNA. This is consistent with an intergenic/non-coding region.

## Feature 3 — Negative results (things that do *not* stand out)

* **No long inverted repeats / hairpins:** no stem ≥24 bp (checked exhaustively to stem ≥40 bp).
* **No long direct repeats** other than the copies in the array.
* **No simple-sequence/low-complexity tracts** beyond a single 6‑bp homopolymer run in each base (A₆ at 666, C₆ at 1,335, G₆ at 2,197, T₆ at 2,675).
* **No common regulatory or repeat signatures** of note: a single `TATAAA` at 1,464 and a single `AATAAA` at 2,818 (plus `AATAAA` reverse-complement matches), `CCAAT` at 905 and 2,887, and a handful of ordinary restriction sites (e.g. KpnI-like `GGTACC` at 288, 626, 1,026, 1,202) — all within chance expectation for 3 kb. No telomeric, Alu-like, or TIR signatures were detected.
* Base composition is unremarkable (GC varies 36–63% in 100‑bp windows, with a locally GC-rich stretch at 1,900–1,960 (63%) immediately 5′ of the array); dinucleotide odds ratios are all 0.90–1.18, with only mild AA/TT elevation.

## Interpretation

The one feature worth flagging is the **~0.5 kb tandem array at 1,962–2,486**, comprising eight copies of `CGGCTTTGGTTACTAAGG`-like 18-mers spaced ~72 bp apart. Its structure — a short, strongly conserved unit embedded in otherwise unrelated sequence — is consistent with either (i) a highly diverged/decayed 72‑bp tandem repeat in which only a ~20‑bp core remains under constraint (e.g. a repeated protein-binding site), or (ii) a repeated ~20‑bp element interspersed at regular intervals into unrelated DNA. Distinguishing these would require comparison with other loci or experimental data, but both interpretations point to a short repeated motif at this position being the functionally interesting element of the region.
